heading_convention: degrees in the plan frame from +x (plan right) toward +y (plan down), clockwise seen from above; three.js front vector = (cos h, 0, sin h); right = h+90, back = h+180, left = h+270
heading_note: No camera heading is stored, so each stop's 'front' bearing was estimated. Method: for every one of the 26 stops the four photos were compared with the floor plan around the stop (entrance doors, reception desk, exterior glazing, Elevators B/C, Stairs B/D, the long east-west corridor, the purple 'Dark Matter' corridor). The rule that fits best is 'front faces the previous-numbered stop' (the photographer walked the main route in descending order, 19 -> 13 -> 10 and 4 -> 1, facing the walking direction); the plain walk-order rule ('front faces the next stop') matched only 4 stops. 13 stops use the rule as is; 13 stops use a visual override (1, 7, 8, 9, 10, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24, 25, 28, 29) such as 'toward Point 9', 'away from Point 24' or a fixed landmark bearing. Bearings are taken toward a point 25 plan units along the graph path; they are not snapped to corridor axes (the look-ahead already follows the corridor). Expect about +/-15 deg error on 'high' stops and +/-30 deg on 'medium' stops (heading_confidence / heading_evidence per stop). Convention: degrees in the plan frame from +x toward +y (clockwise seen from above); photo bearing = heading + 0/90/180/270 for front/right/back/left.
